claim: For every odd \(n>3\), let \(F_n\) be the automaton on \(Q=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) in which \(b\) is the cycle \(1\mapsto2\mapsto\cdots\mapsto n\mapsto1\) and \(a\) fixes \(1,\ldots,n-1\) while sending \(n\) to \(2\). If \(\lambda_n(s)=\min\{|w|:|Qw|\le n-s\}\), then for every \(1\le s\le(n+1)/2\), \(\lambda_n(s)=3s-2\) when \(s\) is odd and \(\lambda_n(s)=3s-3\) when \(s\) is even. For \(s=2r+1\), the word \(a(bab^3a)^r\) attains the bound; for \(s=2r\), the word \(a(bab^3a)^{r-1}ba\) attains it.
integrity: The transition maps, spacing lower bound, explicit hole-set induction, and standalone verifier were checked against the defining \(F_n\) source. Independent audit has not been performed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem determines only the initial half-rank profile, through \(s=(n+1)/2\); later prescribed-rank thresholds are not claimed. Finite power-automaton computations are corroboration only. Literature uniqueness cannot be absolute beyond inspected and indexed sources.
title: Parity-alternating initial rank compression in the automata \(F_n\)
